title: Filtration system efficiency: Impurity removal and residual mass calculation

child-questions.question: Using the provided 'Filtration System Efficiency Test Results' data, System FS-001 consistently removes 90% of initial impurities, whereas System FS-002 consistently removes 80%. If both systems were to process distinct solutions each containing an initial mass of 50 grams of impurities, calculate the absolute difference in the quantity of impurities, in grams, that would be removed by FS-001 compared to FS-002.
child-questions.title: Analysis of Filtration System Impurity Removal Rates
child-questions.solution: "{\"question\": \"Filtration System FS-001 processes an initial amount of impurities as listed in the table. If Filtration System FS-003 were to process an initial amount of impurities that is twice its listed initial amount, while maintaining its removal efficiency, what would be the difference in the remaining impurities between FS-003 (under this new condition) and FS-001?\", \"options\": {\"A\": \"4 grams\", \"B\": \"2 grams\", \"C\": \"8 grams\", \"D\": \"15 grams\", \"E\": \"6 grams\"}, \"solution\": \"Step 1: Analyze given information and identify what needs to be found\\nWe need to determine the difference in the amount of impurities remaining after filtration for System FS-003 (under a modified condition) and System FS-001.\\n\\nFrom the 'Filtration System Efficiency Test Results' table:\\n- For FS-001: Initial Impurities = 20 grams, Percentage Removed = 90%\\n- For FS-003: Initial Impurities = 30 grams, Percentage Removed = 90%\\n\\nThe new condition for FS-003 states that its initial impurities will be twice its listed amount.\\n\\nStep 2: Set up mathematical relationship or logical framework\\nTo find the remaining impurities for any system, we use the formula: Remaining Impurities = Initial Impurities $\\\\times$ (1 - Percentage Removed as a decimal).\\nFirst, calculate the remaining impurities for FS-001.\\nNext, calculate the new initial impurities for FS-003.\\nThen, calculate the remaining impurities for FS-003 using its new initial amount.\\nFinally, find the absolute difference between these two remaining impurity amounts.\\n\\nStep 3: Perform calculations with proper units / Apply reasoning\\n- **For Filtration System FS-001:**\\n  Initial Impurities = 20 grams\\n  Percentage Removed = 90% = 0.90\\n  Remaining Impurities (FS-001) = $20\\\\text{ g} \\\\times (1 - 0.90) = 20\\\\text{ g} \\\\times 0.10 = 2\\\\text{ g}$\\n\\n- **For Filtration System FS-003 (under new condition):**\\n  Original Initial Impurities = 30 grams\\n  New Initial Impurities = $2 \\\\times 30\\\\text{ g} = 60\\\\text{ g}$\\n  Percentage Removed (remains the same) = 90% = 0.90\\n  Remaining Impurities (FS-003 new) = $60\\\\text{ g} \\\\times (1 - 0.90) = 60\\\\text{ g} \\\\times 0.10 = 6\\\\text{ g}$\\n\\n- **Difference in Remaining Impurities:**\\n  Difference = Remaining Impurities (FS-003 new) - Remaining Impurities (FS-001)\\n  Difference = $6\\\\text{ g} - 2\\\\text{ g} = 4\\\\text{ g}$\\n\\nStep 4: Check solution using logical reasoning\\nFor FS-001, 90% removal of 20g means 18g removed, leaving 2g. This is correct.\\nFor FS-003 with double the initial amount, it means 60g initially. 90% removal of 60g means 54g removed, leaving 6g. This is correct.\\nThe difference between 6g and 2g is 4g. The calculations are consistent and logical.\\n\\nStep 5: Confirm solution addresses original question\\nThe final calculation of 4 grams directly answers the question about the difference in remaining impurities between FS-003 (under the new condition) and FS-001.\"}"

child-questions.question: A laboratory is evaluating the projected performance of a new prototype filtration unit, designated FS-006, which is engineered to replicate the high-efficiency characteristics observed in the `Filtration System Efficiency Test Results` for systems FS-001, FS-003, and FS-004. Based on the established quantitative relationship between initial and remaining impurities for these specific high-efficiency systems, determine the net mass of impurities that would be successfully removed by FS-006 if it were to process an initial impurity load of 35 grams. Furthermore, if the operational expenditure for FS-006 is projected at $0.50 per gram of initial impurities processed, calculate the total operational cost for this specific experimental trial.
child-questions.title: Extrapolating Filtration Performance from Efficiency Test Data
child-questions.solution: "The 'Filtration System Efficiency Test Results' table provides data for various systems. A new filtration system, FS-006, is being evaluated. It is known to employ similar advanced filter media and operational principles as systems FS-001, FS-003, and FS-004, which are highly regarded for their consistent high performance across different initial impurity loads. If FS-006 is subjected to a trial with an initial impurity load of 28 grams, what would be the predicted remaining impurity level after filtration? (Note: All tests are conducted at a controlled temperature of 25°C, and system FS-002, though different in design, demonstrates good results for medium impurity loads, but its specifics are not relevant to FS-006's predicted performance)."
